description: Block reading relies on the testforblock **failure message** revealing the block name, and that message format has no official stability guarantee. When a game update changes the wording, or the game language is not Traditional Chinese, Simplified Chinese or English, parsing breaks, and it breaks **silently**. This probe actively checks whether the reading path still works; **run it once before class** to know whether mc_read_block results can be trusted. It does not need to know what is at the spot: if it is air, it asks about bedrock (a guaranteed mismatch) to force a failure message; if something is there, the first question already produced a message. At most two commands, and it never writes to the world. parseable=false means the protocol has drifted, and mc_read_block results cannot be trusted at all.

position.description: Any coordinate works, empty or not

mode.description: absolute = world coordinates; relative = ~ relative to the command source; local = ^ relative to its facing

name: mc_verify_reading

parseable.description: false means the protocol has drifted and block reading cannot be trusted

title: Verify that block reading still works
